top_temples.name: Kali Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Ambala's oldest temples, drawing large crowds during Navratri.

top_temples.name: Bhawani Amba Temple (Sheetla Mata)
top_temples.location_note: Over 200 years old, in the heart of Ambala City; the goddess after whom the city is popularly said to be named.

top_temples.name: Tilla Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Called the largest temple in Haryana, in northwest Ambala; known for its 108-foot Gorakhnath Dhwaj flag and Shivratri celebrations.

top_temples.name: Hathikhana Kailash Temple
top_temples.location_note: 19th-century temple known for its large Ardhanariswar statue.

top_temples.name: Ambika Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Well-known local shrine dedicated to Devi Amba in Ambala.

top_temples.name: Chandi Mandir (Chandi Devi Temple)
top_temples.location_note: On the Chandigarh-Kalka road; a multi-deity complex also honoring Radha Krishna, Shiva, Hanuman, and Ram. Chandigarh's name derives from this temple.

top_temples.name: Mata Mansa Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: A Shakti Peeth just outside Chandigarh in Panchkula, closely associated with the city's temple circuit.

top_temples.name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1989 in the heart of Chandigarh; draws large crowds for evening aarti.

top_temples.name: Jayanti Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the outskirts of Chandigarh, also home to shrines of Ganesha, Shiva, and Lakshmi.

top_temples.name: Sri Karthikeya Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: Among the most notable temples within Chandigarh city.

top_temples.name: Shri Maharani Vaishno Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A revered pilgrimage-style temple complex in Faridabad.

top_temples.name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
top_temples.location_note: Established in 1988 on a 3-acre marble complex.

top_temples.name: Shree Banke Bihari Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Popular Krishna temple in Faridabad.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple
top_temples.location_note: Faridabad branch of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness.

top_temples.name: Prachin Shri Laxmi Narayan Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Faridabad's older Vishnu-Lakshmi temples.

top_temples.name: Sheetla Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Located at Masani Village, Sector 6; devotees believe worship here cures ailments.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple (Sri Sri Radha Damodar)
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1998 at Sudarshan Dham, Sector 67, Badshahpur.

top_temples.name: Digambar Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest temples in Gurgaon, dating to the 17th-century Mughal era.

top_temples.name: Sitaram Temple, Farrukhnagar
top_temples.location_note: Located in Farrukhnagar, notable for its distinctive architecture.

top_temples.name: Sai Ka Angan
top_temples.location_note: One of the most prominent Sai Baba temples in North India.

top_temples.name: Agroha Dham Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1976; known for a 90-foot Hanuman statue and the Shakti Sarovar pond.

top_temples.name: Devi Bhawan Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Prominent Devi temple in Hisar.

top_temples.name: Maa Bhanbhori Bhramri Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Notable pilgrimage site in Hisar.

top_temples.name: Rani Sati Temple
top_temples.location_note: Well-known temple among Hisar's Marwari community.

top_temples.name: Shri Hanuman Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Hisar's popular Hanuman shrines.

top_temples.name: Shri Karneshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Marble temple complex with an old peepal tree where devotees tie red threads to make wishes.

top_temples.name: Shri Mata Durga Bhavani Bada Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Known for ornate marble work and extensive murals.

top_temples.name: Sitamai Temple
top_temples.location_note: Over 500 years old; one of the few temples in India dedicated specifically to Sita.

top_temples.name: Geeta Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Temple centered on the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita.

top_temples.name: Sri Ram Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Karnal's most visited Hindu temples.

top_temples.name: Sthaneshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest temples in Haryana; tradition holds the Pandavas sought Shiva's blessings here before the Mahabharata war.

top_temples.name: Bhadrakali Shaktipeeth Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas of India, believed to mark where Sati's ankle fell.

top_temples.name: Birla Mandir (Geeta Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Prominent temple on the grounds associated with Kurukshetra's Gita heritage.

top_temples.name: Kamal Nabhi Temple (Nabhi Kamal)
top_temples.location_note: Ancient shrine among Kurukshetra's 48-kos pilgrimage circuit.

top_temples.name: Jyotisar Krishna Temple
top_temples.location_note: Marks the site traditionally believed to be where Krishna recited the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.

top_temples.name: Shri Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Built in the 18th century; over 250 years old, very crowded on festival days.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Notable Jagannath temple in Panipat.

top_temples.name: Shree Geeta Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Temple devoted to Bhagavad Gita teachings.

top_temples.name: Radha Krishna Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Popular Krishna-Radha temple in Panipat.

top_temples.name: Shree Ram Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Well-known Ram temple in the city.

top_temples.name: Prithudak (Pirthudakeshwar) Temple
top_temples.deity: Shiva, associated with Saraswati Pitru Tirtha
top_temples.location_note: Built by the Marathas on the banks of the dried-up Saraswati river; the central shrine of Pehowa's identity as Pitrudhak Teerth, an ancient site for ancestral rites (pinda daan) said to predate Gaya and Prayag in sanctity.

top_temples.name: Kartikeya Temple, Pehowa
top_temples.location_note: Ancient, historically documented temple distinct from the main Pitru tirtha shrine, within the same pilgrimage town.

top_temples.name: Durga Bhawan Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Located in Model Town, Rohtak; known for vibrant Navratri celebrations.

top_temples.name: Baba Mast Nath Math
top_temples.location_note: One of Rohtak's most important sites tied to the Nath tradition of Hinduism.

top_temples.name: Sheetla Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Particularly popular during Navratri.

top_temples.name: Shri Digambar Jain Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Main Digambar Jain temple complex in Rohtak, with nine platforms for various deities.

top_temples.name: Shiv Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located in the middle of town; busiest during Shivratri.

top_temples.name: Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Named for its Panchmukhi (five-faced) Hanuman idol.

top_temples.name: Shri Radha Kunj Bihari Temple
top_temples.location_note: ISKCON temple on Hare Krishna Marg in Yamunanagar.

top_temples.name: Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Yamunanagar's oldest sites of Shiva worship.

top_temples.name: Chilta Temple
top_temples.deity: Associated with Mahant Ganga Nand Giri
top_temples.location_note: About 60 years old, tied to a local Nath-tradition sadhu's prayer ground.

top_temples.name: Shani Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Popular Shani Bhagwan temple in Yamunanagar.
